questions.question: Explain in brief:1. Unit heaters 2. Boiler. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• A unit heater is a self-contained, non-ducted device that heats the specific area where it is
  • installed. It uses a fuel source (like natural gas, propane, or electricity) to heat a heat exchanger. A
  • powerful internal fan then blows air over that exchanger and directly into the room.
  • Boilers are the heart of a greenhouse's central heating system, typically chosen for larger
  • commercial operations (over 1,000 m²) or facilities requiring precise temperature control. Unlike
  • unit heaters that blow hot air, boilers use water or steam to transport heat, which is up to 3,500
  • times more efficient at carrying energy than air.

questions.question: Briefly describe the role of active winter cooling system in greenhouse. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Convection Tube Cooling: A fan introduces cold outside air into a plastic tube running along
  • the greenhouse ceiling, allowing the air to warm up slightly before it descends to the plant zone.
  • Horizontal Air Flow (HAF) Fans: Fans are positioned to move air horizontally along the length of
  • the greenhouse, blending cool air from vents with the existing warm air to prevent cold spots.

questions.question: Differentiate training and pruning. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html: • Training Pruning Directing shape and structure (framework). Managing physiological functions and fruit production. Guiding growth via tying, trellising, or staking. Selective removal of plant parts (leaves, stems, suckers). Starts shortly after transplanting to establish a "skeleton". Ongoing throughout the plant's life to maintain health and yield. Improves light penetration and air circulation. Redirects energy (sap flow) from foliage to flowers and fruit.

questions.question: Role of microprocessors and computers in controlling environment inside a greenhouse. / [CO2] [5x5 = 25]
questions.solution_html:
• Microprocessors and computers act as the "brain" of a modern greenhouse, transforming it into a
  • self-regulating ecosystem by continuously monitoring and adjusting environmental variables.
  • Sensors: Gather analog signals .
  • Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC): Converts sensor readings into a digital format the
  • microprocessor can process.
  • Microprocessor/Microcomputer: Executes programmed logic to decide whether to activate
  • or deactivate equipment.
  • Actuators & Relays: Physical components (fans, heaters, sprinklers) that carry out the
  • processor's commands.
